title: Ferroelastic domain wall driven glassy dynamics and photoresponse in a SrTiO$_3$ (111) two-dimensional electron gas
authors: Jyotirmay Maity, Manav Beniwal, Pranab Hazra, Sumit Tomar, Srimanta Middey
abstract: The (111) orientation of SrTiO$_3$ (STO)-based heterostructures has emerged as a versatile platform for two-dimensional electron gases (2DEGs), yet the influence of STO's polar ferroelastic domain-wall (DW) network on charge transport remains largely unexplored. Here we study AlO$_x$/STO (111) interfaces hosting 2DEGs of different carrier densities. In the lower-density 2DEG, low-temperature transport exhibits thermal hysteresis, slow resistance relaxation, cooling-rate dependence, and memory effects, signaling glasslike electron dynamics. The relaxation is strongly non-monotonic in temperature, increasing below $\sim$80 K, peaking near 25 K, and vanishing below $\sim$12 K, tracking the established evolution of the ferroelastic DW state of bulk STO rather than any electronic energy scale, which identifies the DW network as its origin. These signatures are absent in a second, more metallic interface with much higher carrier density, demonstrating that the electron-DW coupling can be tuned. We further show that polar DWs govern the photoresponse: the persistent photoconductivity rises sharply below $\sim$80 K, coinciding with the onset of DW polarity. Together, these results establish polar ferroelastic DWs as a carrier-density-tunable electronic degree of freedom in STO (111)-based 2DEGs, opening routes to manipulate 2DEG properties through topological defects.
summary: This work demonstrates that the ferroelastic domain walls in SrTiO3 (111) act as a controllable, glassy degree of freedom influencing the electronic properties of 2DEGs. By tuning the carrier density, researchers can switch the system between a glassy state dominated by DW dynamics and a more metallic state. This opens avenues for manipulating electronic properties using topological defects.
main_problem: The study investigates how the polar ferroelastic domain-wall (DW) network in SrTiO3 (111) influences charge transport and photoresponse in two-dimensional electron gases (2DEGs).
main_result: The slow, glassy dynamics observed in the 2DEG transport and photoresponse are directly linked to the underlying polar ferroelastic DW network, which acts as a tunable electronic degree of freedom.
method: The research combines low-temperature transport measurements (resistance relaxation, memory effects) with photoresponse measurements on AlOx/STO (111) heterostructures.
model_or_system: The physical system is a 2DEG confined at an AlOx/STO (111) interface. The key element is the ferroelastic domain wall network within the STO substrate, which introduces a polar background field.
key_observables: Thermal hysteresis, slow resistance relaxation, memory effects, and persistent photoconductivity.
important_parameters: Carrier density ($n_s$), temperature (especially the transition region around 80 K and 25 K), and light intensity.
main_assumptions: The slow dynamics observed are attributed to the glassy nature of the ferroelastic DW network, rather than purely electronic energy scales.
figures_summary: Figures show resistance vs. temperature (hysteresis), temporal evolution of resistance (relaxation curves), and photoinduced changes in conductivity, demonstrating history and rate dependence.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares low-density (glassy) vs. high-density (non-glassy) 2DEGs, analyzes the temperature and time dependence of resistance relaxation, and finally links the photoresponse to the onset of DW polarity.
why_interesting: The coupling between topological defects (DWs) and itinerant charge carriers provides a concrete, measurable platform for studying glassy dynamics and emergent order parameters in condensed matter systems.
